name: neurosurgical emergencies overview
title: Neurosurgical emergencies: headache, coma, a new deficit or trauma mean pressure in a closed skull; protect the airway, image, and decompress according to what takes up the space: an epidural or acute subdural hematoma, a ruptured aneurysm, a tumour with edema, or hydrocephalus

root.title: Headache · coma · new neurological deficit · trauma: the cause is PRESSURE
lines: examine to LOCALIZE: Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS), PUPILS, cranial nerves, power side to side, sensory level
INTUBATE for GCS < 9 (airway protection) → image → emergency neurosurgery = DECOMPRESSION

groups.title: BLOOD
lines: which space it is in decides the shape and the outlook

head: h
Epidural hematoma
middle meningeal ARTERY
contact blow to the side of the head
pres: • stunned, then fine, then cannot be woken
• BLOWN PUPIL on the SAME side (third nerve)

head: h
Acute subdural hematoma
BRIDGING VEINS
acceleration-deceleration
tx: outcome UNPREDICTABLE: depends on the brain injury underneath

head: h
Subarachnoid hemorrhage
ruptured ANEURYSM
inv: CT: blood in the subarachnoid space
lumbar puncture: blood in the CSF
tx: • re-rupture 6% day 1, 20% at 2 weeks, 50% at 6 months
• protects against the NEXT bleed only

head: h
Tumour with edema
leaky tumour vessels: VASOGENIC edema
pres: • then a rapid fall in consciousness
tx: restores the blood-brain barrier → edema shrinks
shrinks brain with an INTACT barrier

head: h
Hydrocephalus
e.g. after bacterial meningitis
tx: DIVERT the CSF: untreated it KILLS by herniation
